old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a burning cigarette resting on a textured surface, likely ash or soil. The cigarette is partially consumed, with the filter end showing signs of ash and the paper wrapping beginning to char. As the video progresses, the filter end continues to burn, emitting small wisps of smoke that rise gently into the air. The ash at the tip grows larger and more defined, indicating the ongoing combustion process. The background remains consistently dark, which contrasts sharply with the lighter colors of the cigarette and the ash, making these elements stand out prominently. There are no visible characters or animals in the scene; the focus is entirely on the burning cigarette and its immediate surroundings. The camera maintains a steady position throughout, providing a clear and uninterrupted view of the burning process.

caption: The video captures a close-up of a cigarette resting horizontally on a dark granular surface against a black background. From left to right the object shows a tan cork filter, a band of white paper, a glowing red ember at the burn line, and a column of grey ash. The filter's left end stays fixed at the frame edge throughout, holding the cigarette body in place as the ember flickers at the burn line. For the first part of the excerpt the ash forms a long column that stretches all the way to the right edge. This column then breaks off, leaving only a short ash stub with a pointed tip near the ember and a few small fragments scattered on the surface below. The red ember glows and dims intermittently. Thin wisps of smoke rise sporadically above the burn line.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the

'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.
